offence_category.reason: The offence is murder under s.302 IPC at trial.

statutory_provisions.reason: s.302, s.304 Part I and Exception 1 to s.300 are the core provisions applied.

weapon.reason: A pick-axe was seized on the appellant's disclosure and found blood-stained.

evidence_type.correct_value: Medical, circumstantial (s.106 Evidence Act), and disclosure/recovery evidence; no eyewitness to the killing
evidence_type.quote: did not profess to having made any such statement, or that she had seen the appellant committing the offence
evidence_type.reason: No eyewitness saw the offence; the judgment relies on medical, circumstantial and recovery evidence.

confession.correct_value: Confession inadmissible under s.25; statement admissible only to identify the accused as maker and s.27 discovery portion relating to the pick-axe/body
confession.quote: the confession is inadmissible as proof of confession is prohibited under Section 25
confession.reason: The confession is inadmissible as such; only identification and s.27 discovery parts are admissible.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: The deceased had consumed alcohol and had told the appellant to leave the house and if not, he would kill the appellant
aggravating_circumstances.reason: These are provocation facts the court relied on for mitigation, not aggravating circumstances.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Loss of self-control from grave and sudden provocation and absence of premeditation are the court's stated basis.

trial_court_outcome.reason: The appellant was convicted under s.302 IPC by the trial court.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court affirmed the s.302 conviction (judgment dated 25.02.2019, Criminal Appeal No. 400 of 2013)
high_court_outcome.quote: we are in agreement with the High Court and the trial court
high_court_outcome.reason: The High Court's decision is stated and it agreed with the trial court, not 'not applicable'.

final_outcome.correct_value: Appeal partly allowed; conviction converted from s.302 to s.304 Part I IPC
final_outcome.quote: Applying the provocation exception, we would convert the conviction of the appellant from Section 302 to Part I of Section 304
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' omits that the s.302 conviction was converted to s.304 Part I.

offence_finally_established.reason: The conviction was converted to s.304 Part I, culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Sentence modified to the period already undergone (time served)
imprisonment_type.quote: we are inclined to modify the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone
imprisonment_type.reason: The sentence was reduced to time already served, not a new fixed term.

imprisonment_years.quote: the appellant has already suffered incarceration for over 10 years
imprisonment_years.reason: The judgment says 'over 10 years', not exactly 10.

fine_rs.reason: The judgment imposes a fine of Rs. 1,000/-.

neutral_facts.correct_value: The accused, the deceased's brother, was involved in an incident where the deceased died from head injuries. The deceased was an alcohol addict who abused and threatened the accused. On the night of the incident, the deceased had been drinking and told the accused to leave or he would be killed. The accused was charged under s.302 IPC.
neutral_facts.quote: Therefore, we hold that the acts of provocation on the basis of which the appellant caused the death of his brother, Dashrath Nirmalkar, were both sudden and grave
neutral_facts.reason: Summary states the court's holding on provocation and fine/sentence details, revealing outcome, and contains garbled fragments.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment is the maximum under s.302; minimum for s.304 Part I is not stated; 6 months is only the default term for non-payment of fine
offence_severity.quote: pay fine of Rs.1,000/-, and in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months
offence_severity.reason: Life maximum is supported, but 6 months is the fine default term, not a minimum sentence.

attempt_completion.reason: The deceased died from the injuries, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: The judgment describes coma from shock and multiple skull fractures causing death.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Charged under s.302 IPC; conviction converted to s.304 Part I IPC; separate s.309 attempted suicide charge and sentence also noted
number_of_offences.quote: conviction of the appellant is converted from Section 302 to Part I of Section 304
number_of_offences.reason: The s.304 Part I conviction was converted, not upheld, and the s.309 matter is omitted.

financial_property_loss.reason: No property or financial loss is mentioned in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.reason: The court found sudden provocation and loss of self-control, with no reflection or planning shown.

motive.reason: The prosecution relied on the deceased's alcohol addiction and abusive conduct to show motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: The judgment finds the appellant and deceased were together that night and the chain of circumstances bars any other perpetrator.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Public witnesses were declared hostile but deposed in unison that the two stayed in separate rooms; only PW-9 and PW-10 were present at the time of the incident
witness_credibility.quote: Testimonies of Kumari Shanti Nirmalkar (PW-9) and Kumari Madhu Nirmalkar (PW-10) are important as they were present in the house at the time of the incident
witness_credibility.reason: Presence at the incident applies only to PW-9 and PW-10, not all witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Appellant went to the police station on 26 Sept 2011 and confessed; burn injuries to hands; attempted suicide by holding live electrical wires; s.309 sentence of 10 days
post_offence_conduct.quote: On 26th September, 2011, the appellant himself went to the police station and confessed the crime
post_offence_conduct.reason: Omits the voluntary confession to police, which the judgment treats as relevant conduct.

custody_duration.reason: The appellant has been in custody since 27 September 2011, over 10 years.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not stated in the judgment.

trial_duration.correct_value: High Court judgment dated 25.02.2019; Supreme Court decision dated 02.08.2022; offence date not stated (confession 26.09.2011)

trial_duration.reason: High Court and Supreme Court decision dates are stated in the judgment.

investigation_status.reason: Trial completion is supported, but FIR registration and charge sheet are not mentioned.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court affirmance and Supreme Court conversion to s.304 Part I are all stated.
